summary: Scheme-level étale perverse sheaves, stage EDC.5, at target level. The abstract layer plans what Mathlib's t-structures lack: the abelian heart (through Mathlib's admissible-subcategory criterion), t-cohomology, t-exact functors, recollements, gluing of t-structures, the abstract intermediate extension with the classification of simple objects, and tilting along a torsion theory. On a separated scheme of finite type over any field, with noetherian coefficients killed by an invertible integer, the middle perverse t-structure is defined pointwise by stalks and costalks against dim(x), glued along stratifications and shown independent of choices by smooth-pair purity; its heart Perv(X, Λ) is a stack. Perverse cohomology, open–closed recollement, the shifted local systems on smooth schemes, intermediate extension (image, strict boundary bounds, transitivity, Deligne's truncation formula under its local-constancy hypothesis), the intersection complex with independence of the smooth open, finite length and the simple objects follow. Exactness: quasi-finite, finite and étale maps, fibre-dimension amplitude, smooth pullback with its shift and full faithfulness, perverse Artin vanishing, affine open complements, external products. Verdier duality preserves Perv for self-injective or rational coefficients, with D IC_X(L) ≅ IC_X(L^∨(d)); integrally it exchanges p with the tilt p⁺. ℓ-adic O and E coefficients use the requested ℓ-adic formalism. Semismall pushforward is proved stratum by stratum with compact-support bounds and duality, closing the earlier draft's costalk gap, and small maps give IC. Nonconstructible stalk and costalk conditions serve the Igusa and nearby-cycle consumers. No purity, semisimplicity or decomposition is claimed; no implementation is claimed.

nodes.title: The heart of a t-structure is an abelian category
nodes.statement: Let C be a pretriangulated category satisfying the octahedral axiom (Mathlib's IsTriangulated) and let t be a t-structure on C in Mathlib's sense (aisles t.le n and coaisles t.ge n, with t.le n = t.le 0 shifted by −n). Its heart C^♥ := t.le 0 ∩ t.ge 0, as a full subcategory with inclusion ι, is an abelian category, and ι is additive and fully faithful. Moreover: (i) Hom_C(ιA, (ιB)[m]) = 0 for A, B in the heart and every m < 0; (ii) a sequence 0 → A → B → D → 0 in C^♥ is short exact if and only if there is a morphism ιD → (ιA)[1] completing ιA → ιB → ιD to a distinguished triangle, and that morphism is then unique; (iii) the heart is closed under extensions in C: if X′ → X → X″ → X′[1] is distinguished with X′, X″ in the heart, so is X; (iv) a morphism f : A → B of the heart has kernel ι-image τ_{≤0}(Cone(f)[−1]) and cokernel τ_{≥0}Cone(f) computed with Mathlib's truncation functors.
hypotheses: C pretriangulated with the octahedral axiom; t any t-structure (no boundedness or nondegeneracy is needed).
The abelian structure is the one supplied by Mathlib's AbelianSubcategory criterion; the theorem is that its two hypotheses hold for the heart.
proofSteps: Negative Hom vanishing (i): (ιB)[m] lies in t.ge (−m) ⊆ t.ge 1 for m < 0, so every map from t.le 0 to it is zero by the orthogonality axiom of the t-structure (BBD 1.3.1 (i)).

Admissibility: for f : A → B in the heart complete ιA → ιB to a triangle ιA → ιB → S → (ιA)[1]. The rotated triangle ιB → S → (ιA)[1] shows S ∈ t.le 0 ∩ t.ge (−1). The truncation triangle τ_{≤−1}S → S → τ_{≥0}S gives K := (τ_{≤−1}S)[−1] and Q := τ_{≥0}S in the heart with a distinguished triangle K[1] → S → Q → K[2], which is Mathlib's admissibleMorphism condition (BBD 1.3.6 proof, p.31; the diagram (1.2.2.1)).

The heart is closed under finite direct sums because both t.le 0 and t.ge 0 are closed under extensions (BBD 1.3.4, p.30: each is an orthogonal of the other), hence has finite products. Apply mathlib:CategoryTheory.Triangulated.AbelianSubcategory.abelian to ι.

(ii) and (iv) are the description of kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences in an admissible abelian subcategory (BBD 1.2.4–1.2.5, the admissibility used in 1.3.6); (iii) is BBD 1.3.6's stability under extensions, again from 1.3.4.
acceptance: For Mathlib's canonical t-structure DerivedCategory.TStructure.t on D(A), the heart is equivalent to A through the degree-zero inclusion (BBD 1.3.6, Exemple, p.31).
For the middle perverse t-structure on a point Spec Ω with Ω separably closed, the heart is the category of finitely generated Λ-modules in degree 0 (EDC.5/perverse-sheaf-category).

Non-example: in D(Ab), the full subcategory of complexes with cohomology in degrees −1 and 0 is not the heart of any t-structure: it contains A = (ℤ/2)[1] and B = ℤ/2, and Hom(B, A[−1]) = Hom(ℤ/2, ℤ/2) ≠ 0, which (i) forbids.

sources.locator: Théorème 1.3.6 and its proof, pp.31–32; 1.3.4, p.30
sources.match: The heart of a t-category is an admissible abelian subcategory stable by extensions; its proof shows every morphism of the heart is admissible by truncating the cone.

nodes.title: The cohomology functors of a t-structure
nodes.statement: Let t be a t-structure on a pretriangulated category C with the octahedral axiom. The zeroth t-cohomology is H⁰_t := τ_{≥0} ∘ τ_{≤0} : C → C^♥, lifted to the heart (canonically isomorphic to τ_{≤0} ∘ τ_{≥0}, BBD 1.3.5), and H^m_t(X) := H⁰_t(X[m]). Then: (a) H⁰_t is a homological functor to the abelian heart: a distinguished triangle X → Y → Z → X[1] gives a long exact sequence … → H^m_t X → H^m_t Y → H^m_t Z → H^{m+1}_t X → …; (b) for X in the heart, H⁰_t X ≅ X and H^m_t X = 0 for m ≠ 0; (c) if X lies in t.le a ∩ t.ge b for some a, b (X is t-bounded) then X ≅ 0 if and only if H^m_t X = 0 for all m, and X ∈ t.le 0 if and only if H^m_t X = 0 for all m > 0 (dually for t.ge 0); (d) if t is nondegenerate (⋂ t.le n = ⋂ t.ge n = 0) the same detection holds for every object (BBD 1.3.7).
hypotheses: C pretriangulated with the octahedral axiom; t a t-structure. Detection (c) needs t-boundedness of X; (d) needs nondegeneracy.
proofSteps: Define H⁰_t from Mathlib's truncation functors t.truncLE 0 and t.truncGE 0; the composite lands in the heart because truncations preserve the opposite aisle (BBD 1.3.4–1.3.5), and lift it along the inclusion.
Homological: BBD 1.3.6, second half (pp.31–32): first for triangles inside t.ge 0 and inside t.le 0 by representability, then the general case by the octahedral axiom.
(b): truncations of an object of the heart are itself. (c): induction on b − a with the triangles τ_{≤b−1}X → X → H^b_t(X)[−b]; (d): BBD 1.3.7.
acceptance: For Mathlib's canonical t-structure on D(Ab): H¹_t((ℤ/2)[−1]) ≅ ℤ/2 and H⁰_t((ℤ/2)[−1]) = 0.
For the middle perverse t-structure, H^m_t is perverse cohomology pH^m (EDC.5/perverse-sheaf-category); on a smooth curve C, pH^{1}(Λ_C) ≅ Λ_C[1] and pH^m(Λ_C) = 0 for m ≠ 1.

nodes.title: Left and right t-exact functors
nodes.statement: Let (C₁, t₁), (C₂, t₂) be pretriangulated categories with t-structures and T : C₁ → C₂ a triangulated functor. T is right t-exact if T(t₁.le 0) ⊆ t₂.le 0, left t-exact if T(t₁.ge 0) ⊆ t₂.ge 0, and t-exact if both; since T commutes with shifts, right t-exactness gives T(t₁.le n) ⊆ t₂.le n for every n, and dually. The induced functor on hearts is pT := H⁰_{t₂} ∘ T ∘ ι₁ : C₁^♥ → C₂^♥. Then (BBD 1.3.17): (i) pT is right exact if T is right t-exact and left exact if T is left t-exact; (ii) for T right t-exact and K ∈ t₁.le 0, H⁰_{t₂}(TK) ≅ pT(H⁰_{t₁}K) (dually for left t-exact and K ∈ t₁.ge 0); (iii) for an adjunction T* ⊣ T_* of triangulated functors, T* is right t-exact if and only if T_* is left t-exact, and then pT* ⊣ pT_*; (iv) composites of left (right) t-exact functors are left (right) t-exact and p(T₂ ∘ T₁) ≅ pT₂ ∘ pT₁. A fully faithful t-exact functor reflects the aisles (BBD 1.3.19).
hypotheses: Triangulated functors between pretriangulated categories with t-structures; (iii) needs an adjunction of triangulated functors (Mathlib Adjunction plus IsTriangulated on both functors).
proofSteps: Definitions by the two inclusions; the shift statement from T(X[1]) ≅ T(X)[1] and t.le n = t.le 0 [−n].
(i), (ii): long exact sequences of H_{t₂} applied to T of a short exact sequence of the heart, using EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory (ii) (BBD 1.3.17 proof, p.37).
(iii): Hom(T*V, U) = Hom(V, T_*U) and the characterisation of t.le 0 as the left orthogonal of t.ge 1 (BBD 1.3.4); the heart adjunction from H⁰ of the adjunction maps (BBD 1.3.17 (iii), 1.3.18).
(iv): BBD 1.3.17 (iv) from (ii).
acceptance: The identity of C is t-exact; the shift [1] is right t-exact for every t.
For an exact functor F : A → B of abelian categories, the derived functor D(A) → D(B) is t-exact for the canonical t-structures.

nodes.title: Recollement of triangulated categories
nodes.statement: A recollement D_F → D → D_U consists of pretriangulated categories D_F, D, D_U, triangulated functors i_* : D_F → D and j^* : D → D_U, triangulated adjoints i^* ⊣ i_* ⊣ i^! and j_! ⊣ j^* ⊣ j_* (all six triangulated, with the four adjunctions given), such that (a) j^* ∘ i_* ≅ 0; (b) for every K in D the adjunction maps extend to distinguished triangles j_!j^*K → K → i_*i^*K → (j_!j^*K)[1] and i_*i^!K → K → j_*j^*K → (i_*i^!K)[1]; (c) the adjunction maps i^*i_* → 1, 1 → i^!i_*, 1 → j^*j_!, j^*j_* → 1 are isomorphisms, so i_*, j_! and j_* are fully faithful (BBD 1.4.3). Consequences: i^*j_! ≅ 0, i^!j_* ≅ 0, Hom(j_!B, i_*A) = 0 = Hom(i_*A, j_*B); the connecting maps of the triangles in (b) are unique; i_* identifies D_F with the full subcategory of D on which j^* vanishes. The basic instance is constructible étale sheaves on X with a closed subscheme Z and open complement U, with i_* = i_! and j^! = j^* (EDC.1:biduality/recollement-adjunctions).
hypotheses: D_F, D, D_U pretriangulated; the six functors triangulated; adjunctions part of the data.
proofSteps: Record the functors and adjunctions as data, and (a)–(c) as properties (BBD 1.4.3, (1.4.3.1)–(1.4.3.5)).
i^*j_! ≅ 0 and i^!j_* ≅ 0 by adjunction from (a); uniqueness of the connecting maps because Hom(j_!j^*K, i_*i^*K[−1]) = 0 (BBD 1.1.10 with (1.4.3.3)).
The kernel of j^* is the essential image of i_*: the second triangle of (b) for K with j^*K = 0.

nodes.title: Gluing t-structures along a recollement
nodes.statement: Let D_F → D → D_U be a recollement (EDC.5/recollement-situation) of categories satisfying the octahedral axiom, with t-structures t_F and t_U. Put D^{≤0} := {K : j^*K ∈ D_U^{≤0}, i^*K ∈ D_F^{≤0}} and D^{≥0} := {K : j^*K ∈ D_U^{≥0}, i^!K ∈ D_F^{≥0}}. Then: (a) (D^{≤0}, D^{≥0}) is a t-structure on D, the glued t-structure (BBD 1.4.10); conversely a t-structure on D is glued from t-structures on D_U and D_F exactly when j_!j^* is right t-exact (BBD 1.4.12); (b) j_!, i^* are right t-exact, j_*, i^! are left t-exact, j^*, i_* are t-exact, and (pj_!, pj^*, pj_*), (pi^*, pi_*, pi^!) are adjoint triples of functors between the hearts (BBD 1.4.16); (c) on hearts pj^* ∘ pi_* = 0, pi^* ∘ pj_! = 0, pi^! ∘ pj_* = 0, and for A in the heart C the sequences pj_!pj^*A → A → pi_*pi^*A → 0 and 0 → pi_*pi^!A → A → pj_*pj^*A are exact; the essential image of pi_* is the thick subcategory of A with pj^*A = 0, and pj^* identifies C_U with the quotient C/C_F (BBD 1.4.17–1.4.18); (d) for A in C there are exact sequences 0 → pi_*H^{−1}(i^*A) → pj_!pj^*A → A → pi_*pi^*A → 0 and 0 → pi_*pi^!A → A → pj_*pj^*A → pi_*H¹(i^!A) → 0 (BBD 1.4.19); (e) for B in D_U and p ∈ ℤ there is, up to unique isomorphism, a unique extension X of B (j^*X ≅ B) with i^*X ∈ D_F^{≤p−1} and i^!X ∈ D_F^{≥p+1}, namely the relative truncation τ^F_{≤p−1}j_*B (BBD 1.4.14); (f) the glued t-structure is nondegenerate iff t_U and t_F are (1.4.11), and it is bounded when t_U and t_F are bounded.
hypotheses: A recollement whose three categories satisfy the octahedral axiom; t-structures t_U, t_F.
proofSteps: Orthogonality: for X ∈ D^{≤0}, Y ∈ D^{≥1} use the first triangle of X and adjunction: Hom(i_*i^*X, Y) = Hom(i^*X, i^!Y) = 0 and Hom(j_!j^*X, Y) = Hom(j^*X, j^*Y) = 0 (BBD 1.4.10, axiom (i)).

Truncation triangles: choose Y → X → j_*τ_{≥1}j^*X and A → Y → i_*τ_{≥1}i^*Y and apply the octahedral axiom; applying j^*, i^*, i^! to the octahedron shows A ∈ D^{≤0}, B ∈ D^{≥1} (BBD 1.4.10, axiom (iii), pp.48–49).

(b) from the definitions and the adjoint criterion of EDC.5/t-exact-functors (BBD 1.4.16); (c)–(d) from the two triangles of the recollement and long exact sequences of t-cohomology (EDC.5/t-structure-cohomology; BBD 1.4.17–1.4.19).

(e): the triangle i_*i^*X → j_!B[1] ... of BBD 1.4.14 shows any such X is τ^F_{≤p−1}j_*B, which has the required bounds; (f) boundedness: if B ∈ D_U^{[a,b]} and the F-part is bounded, the defining conditions are met in a finite range.

nodes.title: Intermediate extension in a recollement
nodes.statement: In a recollement with glued t-structure (EDC.5/gluing-t-structures), with hearts C_U, C, C_F, the intermediate extension j_!* : C_U → C sends B to the image, in the abelian category C, of the map pj_!B → pj_*B adjoint to the identity of B (BBD 1.4.22). Then: (a) j^*j_!*B ≅ B; (b) j_!*B ≅ τ^F_{≤−1}j_*B ≅ τ^F_{≥1}j_!B, and similarly pj_!B ≅ τ^F_{≤−2}j_*B, pj_*B ≅ τ^F_{≤0}j_*B (BBD 1.4.23); (c) j_!*B is the unique extension X of B in D with i^*X ∈ D_F^{≤−1} and i^!X ∈ D_F^{≥1} (BBD 1.4.24), equivalently the unique extension of B in C with no nonzero subobject or quotient in the essential image of pi_* (BBD 1.4.25); (d) j_!* is a fully faithful functor and sends simple objects to simple objects; (e) every simple object of C is either pi_*S with S simple in C_F or j_!*S with S simple in C_U (BBD 1.4.26).
hypotheses: A recollement of categories satisfying the octahedral axiom with the glued t-structure.
proofSteps: Define j_!* as the image of the canonical map pj_!B → pj_*B in the abelian heart (EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory), the map being H⁰ of j_!B → j_*B (BBD (1.4.6.2), (1.4.22.1)).
(b): BBD 1.4.23 from 1.4.14 (EDC.5/gluing-t-structures (e)) with p = −1, −2, 0.
(c): 1.4.24 is 1.4.14 for p = 0; 1.4.25 reformulates it, because pi^*X (resp. pi^!X) is the largest quotient (resp. subobject) of X in C_F (BBD 1.4.17.1).

(d): a map φ : B → B′ induces a map of images; restriction is faithful on objects with no C_F-sub or quotient because kernel and cokernel defects would be supported on F (1.4.25); simple objects by 1.4.26.
(e): BBD 1.4.26 — a simple object of C either lies in the thick subcategory C_F or has simple image in C/C_F and no sub or quotient in C_F.

nodes.title: Tilting a t-structure along a torsion theory
nodes.statement: Let t be a t-structure on a pretriangulated category D with heart C, and (T, F) a torsion theory on C (Hom(T, F) = 0 for T ∈ T, F ∈ F, and every A in C has a short exact sequence 0 → A_T → A → A_F → 0 with A_T ∈ T, A_F ∈ F). The tilt t⁺ is defined by t⁺.le 0 := {X ∈ t.le 1 : H¹_t X ∈ T} and t⁺.ge 0 := {X ∈ t.ge 0 : H⁰_t X ∈ F}. Then t⁺ is a t-structure on D with t.le 0 ⊆ t⁺.le 0 ⊆ t.le 1 and t.ge 1 ⊆ t⁺.ge 0 ⊆ t.ge 0; its heart C⁺ carries the torsion theory (F, T[−1]); tilting t⁺ along it gives t shifted by one. If C is O-linear (O a discrete valuation ring with uniformizer λ) and noetherian, then (λ-power-torsion objects, objects on which λ is a monomorphism) is a torsion theory on C; if C is artinian, (divisible objects, torsion objects) is one.
hypotheses: D pretriangulated with the octahedral axiom; (T, F) a torsion theory on the heart.
proofSteps: Orthogonality: for X ∈ t⁺.le 0, Y ∈ t⁺.ge 1, Hom(X, Y) = Hom(τ_{≥1}X, τ_{≤1}Y) = Hom_C(H¹X, H¹Y) = 0 since H¹X ∈ T and H¹Y ∈ F (Juteau Prop. 1.3.6 (i)).
Truncation: split H¹_t X by the torsion sequence and lift it to a triangle with BBD 1.3.15 (Juteau Prop. 1.3.6 (iii)).
The noetherian/artinian torsion theories: the chain ker(λ^n) stabilises (resp. im(λ^n)) (Juteau Props. 1.3.4–1.3.5).
acceptance: For D = D^b_fg(ℤ_ℓ) with the natural t-structure and (torsion, torsion-free), the heart of t⁺ contains ℤ_ℓ[0] and (ℤ/ℓ)[−1] but not (ℤ/ℓ)[0]; this is BBD's t-structure on D_c(pt, ℤ) in 3.3.1.

nodes.title: The dimension of a point and the middle perversity
nodes.statement: Let X be a scheme locally of finite type over a field k. For a point x of X put dim(x) := the Krull dimension of the closure of {x} in X, a natural number equal to the transcendence degree of κ(x) over k. The function x ↦ dim(x) is a dimension function: if x specializes to y ≠ x then dim(y) < dim(x), and dim(y) = dim(x) − 1 when {y}^− has codimension one in {x}^−. It does not change under passage to an open (or étale) neighbourhood of x, nor under a purely inseparable or other algebraic extension of the base field at points lying over x; for a morphism f : X → Y of finite type whose fibres have dimension ≤ d, dim(x) ≤ dim(f(x)) + d, with equality dim(x) = dim(f(x)) when f is quasi-finite. The middle perversity is the function p(x) := −dim(x). It is defined through dimension and not codimension: for strata whose closures have different dimensions the two conventions differ.
hypotheses: X locally of finite type over a field (so points have finite transcendence degree and X is catenary).
dim(x) is computed in X, not in a stratum: for x in a locally closed S ⊂ X the closure of x in S and in X have the same dimension.
proofSteps: Define dim(x) as Mathlib's topologicalKrullDim of the closure of {x} (an element of ℕ ∪ {±∞}, finite here); the equality with tr.deg_k κ(x) is the dimension theory of finite-type algebras over a field, applied to the integral closed subscheme {x}^− (BBD 4.0, p.102 uses this as the definition).
Dimension function: {y}^− ⊊ {x}^− are integral of finite type over k, so dim drops, by one in codimension one (catenarity of finite-type algebras over a field).

Open/étale invariance: the closure of x in an open U is dense in the closure in X; étale maps are quasi-finite and preserve transcendence degree. Field extensions: for an algebraic k′/k, residue fields of points over x are algebraic over κ(x).
Morphisms: for y = f(x), κ(x) is a finitely generated extension of κ(y) of transcendence degree at most the dimension of the fibre (BBD 4.2.4, p.108: dim(x) ≤ dim f(x) + d), zero for quasi-finite f.
acceptance: A closed point of 𝔸^n_k has dim 0; the generic point of 𝔸^n_k has dim n.
On X = 𝔸² ⊔ 𝔸¹ the closed points all have dim 0 although they have codimension 2 and 1 respectively.

nodes.title: The middle perverse t-structure on constructible complexes
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, n invertible in k, X separated of finite type over k and Λ a noetherian ring with nΛ = 0. For a point x of X let i_x : x → X be the inclusion, factored as x → {x}^− → X, and put i_x^* K := (K restricted to x) and i_x^! K := (i^!K restricted to the generic point x of {x}^−) for i : {x}^− → X closed; their geometric fibres at x̄ are the stalk and costalk of K at x. Define pD^{≤0}(X, Λ) := {K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ) : ℋ^m(i_x^*K) = 0 for m > −dim(x), for every point x} (4.0.1), equivalently dim Supp ℋ^m(K) ≤ −m for every m (4.0.1′), and pD^{≥0}(X, Λ) := {K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ) : ℋ^m(i_x^!K) = 0 for m < −dim(x), for every point x} (4.0.2), with pD^{≤a} := pD^{≤0}[−a] and pD^{≥a} := pD^{≥0}[−a]. Then (pD^{≤0}, pD^{≥0}) is a t-structure on D^b_c(X, Λ), the middle perverse t-structure. It is bounded: D^{≤−dim X} ⊆ pD^{≤0} ⊆ D^{≤0} and D^{≥0} ⊆ pD^{≥0} ⊆ D^{≥−dim X} for the natural t-structure. For a finite partition of X into equidimensional locally closed strata S, each smooth after passing to the perfect closure of k, such that every ℋ^m(i_S^*K) and ℋ^m(i_S^!K) is locally constant, K ∈ pD^{≤0} iff ℋ^m(i_S^*K) = 0 for m > −dim S on every stratum, and K ∈ pD^{≥0} iff ℋ^m(i_S^!K) = 0 for m < −dim S on every stratum. nodes.title: Perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: In the situation of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure, the category of perverse sheaves is the heart Perv(X, Λ) := pD^{≤0}(X, Λ) ∩ pD^{≥0}(X, Λ), a full abelian subcategory of D^b_c(X, Λ) (EDC.5/heart-abelian-subcategory), with perverse cohomology functors pH^m : D^b_c(X, Λ) → Perv(X, Λ) (EDC.5/t-structure-cohomology). Short exact sequences of perverse sheaves are the distinguished triangles with perverse vertices; Hom(K, L[m]) = 0 for perverse K, L and m < 0. Perverse sheaves form a stack for the étale topology: for perverse K, L the presheaf U ↦ Hom(K|_U, L|_U) on X_ét is a sheaf, and perverse sheaves given on an étale covering with isomorphisms on overlaps satisfying the cocycle condition glue to a perverse sheaf, unique up to unique isomorphism (BBD 2.1.21–2.1.23, 2.2.19). If K is perverse with support of dimension ≤ e, then at every point x with dim(x) = e its stalk is concentrated in degree −e.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
proofSteps: Define Perv(X, Λ) as the heart and pH^m as the t-cohomology of EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure.
Morphism descent: for K ∈ pD^{≤0} and L ∈ pD^{≥0}, ℋ^mRHom(K, L) = 0 for m < 0 (BBD 2.1.20–2.1.21, (2.2.8) in the étale setting), so ℋ⁰RHom(K, L) is the sheaf of morphisms (2.1.22).

Object descent: BBD 2.2.19 gives a proof valid for the étale constructible categories: glue along a finite étale covering using the vanishing of negative local Exts and the morphism descent just proved.

Generic concentration: the support condition gives vanishing above −e at x; on a dense open V of {x}^− smooth of dimension e on which K has lisse cohomology, the costalk condition at x reads ℋ^m(K)_x̄ = 0 for m < −e (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse), since i_x^! and i_x^* differ there by the twist and shift of purity.

nodes.title: Shifted local systems on smooth schemes are perverse
nodes.statement: Let X be smooth over k of pure dimension d and K ∈ D^b_c(X, Λ) with locally constant cohomology sheaves. Then K ∈ pD^{≤0} iff ℋ^m(K) = 0 for m > −d, and K ∈ pD^{≥0} iff ℋ^m(K) = 0 for m < −d. In particular L[d] is perverse for every locally constant constructible sheaf L of Λ-modules, and on lisse complexes the perverse t-structure is the natural t-structure shifted by d. For a point x with dim(x) = d − c, i_x^!K ≅ i_x^*K(−c)[−2c].
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
X smooth over k of pure dimension d; the cohomology sheaves of K are locally constant.
proofSteps: Stalk side: the support of a nonzero locally constant sheaf is a union of components of dimension d, so (4.0.1′) is the vanishing above −d.

Costalk side: choose a smooth dense open V of {x}^− (after passing to k^perf, EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure); V ⊂ X is a smooth pair of codimension c, and smooth-pair purity with locally constant coefficients (EDC.3/smooth-pair-purity) gives i_V^!K ≅ i_V^*K(−c)[−2c]; restrict to x. The costalk condition at x becomes ℋ^m(K_x̄) = 0 for m < −dim(x) − 2c = −d − c, implied by the condition at the generic points (c = 0).
This is the argument of BBD 4.3.2 (p.112–113) and the example in 4.0 (p.102).

nodes.title: Open–closed recollement of perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let i : Z → X be a closed immersion with open complement j : U → X. The middle perverse t-structure on D^b_c(X, Λ) is glued (EDC.5/gluing-t-structures) from those of U and Z along the étale recollement. Consequently: j_!, i^* are right t-exact; Rj_*, i^! are left t-exact; j^* and i_* are t-exact; pj_!, pj^*, pj_* and pi^*, pi_*, pi^! are adjoint triples on perverse sheaves; i_* : Perv(Z, Λ) → Perv(X, Λ) is fully faithful with essential image the perverse sheaves K with j^*K = 0, a thick (Serre) subcategory, and pj^* identifies Perv(U, Λ) with the quotient; for K perverse there are exact sequences of perverse sheaves 0 → i_*pH^{−1}(i^*K) → pj_!j^*K → K → i_*pH⁰(i^*K) → 0 and 0 → i_*pH⁰(i^!K) → K → pj_*j^*K → i_*pH¹(i^!K) → 0, the middle maps being pH⁰ of the counit j_!j^*K → K and the unit K → Rj_*j^*K. No bound i^*K ∈ pD^{[−1,0]} holds for a general closed immersion (that is the affine-open case, EDC.5/affine-open-complement-exactness).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.

Exactness and adjoint triples: EDC.5/gluing-t-structures (b) (BBD 1.4.16, 2.1.6).
Thick subcategory and quotient: EDC.5/gluing-t-structures (c) (BBD 1.4.17.1–1.4.18).
Exact sequences: EDC.5/gluing-t-structures (d) (BBD 1.4.19), using only i^*K ∈ pD^{≤0}, i^!K ∈ pD^{≥0}.

nodes.title: Verdier duality preserves perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let Λ be self-injective (a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ char k, O/λ^m or ℤ/ℓ^m), or Λ = E/ℚ_ℓ finite under the ℓ-adic hypotheses. Verdier duality D_X = RHom(−, K_X) (EDC.1:adjoint/verdier-dual) maps pD^{≤0}(X, Λ) onto pD^{≥0}(X, Λ) and pD^{≥0} onto pD^{≤0}. Hence D_X restricts to an anti-equivalence Perv(X, Λ)^op ≃ Perv(X, Λ) with D_X² ≅ id, pH^m(D_X K) ≅ D_X pH^{−m}(K), D_X ∘ pj_! ≅ pj_* ∘ D_U and D_X ∘ j_!* ≅ j_!* ∘ D_U for an open or locally closed j. For X irreducible of dimension d with a dense open U smooth over k and L locally constant constructible on U, D_X IC_X(L) ≅ IC_X(L^∨(d)) with L^∨ := Hom(L, Λ). No isomorphism IC_X(L) ≅ D_X IC_X(L) is asserted without a given perfect pairing L ⊗ L → Λ(−d). For Λ = O_E (not self-injective) duality exchanges the middle perversity p with p⁺ instead (EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).

The categories D^b_c(X, O) and D^b_c(X, E) and their operations are the ℓ-adic formalism requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2. (only for the E-coefficient case).

nodes.title: Quasi-finite, finite and étale morphisms and the perverse t-structure
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a quasi-finite morphism of separated schemes of finite type over k. Then Rf_! and f^* are right t-exact and their right adjoints Rf_* and f^! are left t-exact for the middle perverse t-structures. If f is finite, f_* = Rf_* = Rf_! is t-exact; if f is étale, f^* = f^! is t-exact; a closed immersion i gives a t-exact fully faithful i_* on perverse sheaves. For a perverse sheaf F on X, Rf_!F ∈ pD^{≤0}(Y) and Rf_*F ∈ pD^{≥0}(Y), and f_!*F := image(pH⁰Rf_!F → pH⁰Rf_*F) defines a functor Perv(X, Λ) → Perv(Y, Λ) generalising j_!*.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
f quasi-finite (for Rf_!: separated, of finite type).
proofSteps: Right t-exactness of Rf_! and f^*: by (4.0.1′) the upper aisle is a condition on dim Supp ℋ^m; for f quasi-finite the underived f_! and f^* are exact, ℋ^m(Rf_!K) = f_!ℋ^m(K) with support f(Supp ℋ^mK) of the same dimension, and Supp ℋ^m(f^*K) = f^{−1}(Supp ℋ^mK) has dimension at most that of Supp ℋ^mK (EDC.5/point-dimension-function) (BBD 2.2.5).

Finite f: Rf_* = Rf_! = f_* exact on sheaves (finite pushforward, imported with proper base change through SF.2), so both one-sided statements combine; étale f: f^! = f^* (EDC.1:adjoint/exceptional-inverse-image) (BBD 2.2.6).

nodes.title: Perverse amplitude of the operations for a morphism with bounded fibre dimension
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a morphism of separated schemes of finite type over k whose fibres have dimension ≤ d. Then f^* maps pD^{≤0}(Y) into pD^{≤d}(X) and f^! maps pD^{≥0}(Y) into pD^{≥−d}(X); Rf_! maps pD^{≤0}(X) into pD^{≤d}(Y) and Rf_* maps pD^{≥0}(X) into pD^{≥−d}(Y). For f proper, Rf_* = Rf_! has perverse amplitude [−d, d]. Consequently (pH^d Rf_!, pH^{−d} f^!) and (pH^d f^*, pH^{−d} Rf_*) are adjoint pairs of functors between perverse sheaves.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
Fibres of f of dimension ≤ d.
proofSteps: f^*: by (4.0.1) and dim(x) ≤ dim f(x) + d (EDC.5/point-dimension-function), ℋ^m(f^*K)_x = ℋ^m(K)_{f(x)} vanishes for m > −dim f(x) ≥ −dim(x) + d (BBD 4.2.4).
Rf_*: adjoint to f^*[d] up to shift (EDC.5/t-exact-functors (iii)).

Rf_! and f^!: duality exchanges each pair for self-injective coefficients (EDC.5/perverse-verdier-self-duality); for a general noetherian Λ use instead the stalk formula of Rf_! (compact-support cohomology of fibres vanishing above 2·dim, EDC.0/compact-pushforward-amplitude-and-colimits) with (4.0.1′), and adjunction for f^!.
The adjunctions on perverse sheaves follow from BBD 1.3.17 (iii) applied to (Rf_![d], f^![−d]) and (f^*[d], Rf_*[−d]).
acceptance: For f : 𝔸¹ → Spec k (d = 1) and K = Λ[1]: Rf_*K = RΓ(𝔸¹, Λ)[1] = Λ[1] ∈ pD^{≥−1} and Rf_!K = Λ(−1)[−1] ∈ pD^{≤1}; both bounds are attained.
For f = P¹ → Spec k (proper, d = 1): Rf_*Λ[1] has perverse cohomology in degrees −1 and 1 only.

sources.match: For fibres of dimension ≤ d the amplitude of f_!, f^* is ≤ d and of f^!, f_* is ≥ −d; duality and the adjoint criterion reduce everything to f^*, where it follows from (4.0.1) and dim(x) ≤ dim f(x) + d; the resulting adjunctions between perverse sheaves; the proper case.

nodes.title: Smooth pullback with its dimension shift
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be smooth of pure relative dimension d. Then f^![−d] ≅ f^*[d](d), and the functor f^*[d] is t-exact for the middle perverse t-structures, inducing an exact functor f^*[d] : Perv(Y, Λ) → Perv(X, Λ) with left adjoint pH^d Rf_!(d) and right adjoint pH^{−d} Rf_*. If moreover f is surjective with geometrically connected fibres, then f^*[d] : Perv(Y, Λ) → Perv(X, Λ) is fully faithful (BBD 4.2.5); for Λ a field its essential image is closed under subobjects and quotients, every perverse sheaf on X has a largest perverse subsheaf and a largest perverse quotient coming from Y, namely f^*[d] of pH^{−d}Rf_* and of pH^dRf_!(d) (BBD 4.2.6.2), and f^*[d] sends simple objects to simple objects.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
f smooth of pure relative dimension d; for full faithfulness, f surjective with geometrically connected fibres; for the thick-image statement Λ is a field (finite of characteristic ℓ, or E).
proofSteps: Smooth purity f^! ≅ f^*(d)[2d] (EDC.2:trace-purity/smooth-purity), so f^*[d] ≅ f^![−d](−d); EDC.5/fibre-dimension-perverse-amplitude gives f^*[d] right t-exact and f^![−d] left t-exact; together t-exact.

Full faithfulness: f^*RHom(K, L) ≅ RHom(f^*K, f^*L) for smooth f (smooth base change, imported through SF.2); for perverse K, L both RHoms lie in D^{≥0}, and f_*f^*H ≅ H for every sheaf H because f has local sections and geometrically connected fibres (BBD (4.2.5.1)–(4.2.5.3)).

Thick image: BBD 4.2.6–4.2.6.2: finite length (EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification) and preservation of simple objects, the latter by smooth base change for j_!* and irreducibility of pulled-back local systems on connected fibres.
acceptance: For pr : 𝔸¹ × Y → Y, pr^*[1] sends IC_Y to IC_{𝔸¹×Y} and is fully faithful on perverse sheaves.

For the étale double cover f : 𝔾_m → 𝔾_m, z ↦ z² (char k ≠ 2, ℓ ≠ 2; fibres not connected), f^*[1] is not full: for the nontrivial quadratic Kummer sheaf L, Hom(Λ[1], L[1]) = 0 while f^*L ≅ Λ gives Hom(f^*Λ[1], f^*L[1]) ≅ Λ.

sources.locator: 4.2.4 (smooth case), pp.108–109; Proposition 4.2.5, p.109; 4.2.6, Lemme 4.2.6.1 and Corollaire 4.2.6.2, pp.110–111

nodes.title: Perverse Artin vanishing for affine morphisms
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be an affine morphism of separated schemes of finite type over k. Then Rf_* : D^b_c(X, Λ) → D^b_c(Y, Λ) is right t-exact and Rf_! is left t-exact for the middle perverse t-structures (BBD 4.1.1–4.1.2); pf_* := pH⁰Rf_* is right exact and pf_! := pH⁰Rf_! left exact on perverse sheaves, and p(fg)_* ≅ pf_* pg_* for affine f, g. If f is quasi-finite and affine, Rf_* and Rf_! are t-exact (BBD 4.1.3). If k is separably closed and K ∈ pD^{≤0}(X), then H^m(Z, K) = 0 for m > 0 for every quasi-finite u : Z → X with Z affine (BBD 4.1.5); in particular for X affine and K perverse, H^m(X, K) = 0 for m > 0 and H^m_c(X, K) = 0 for m < 0, and H^m(X, F) = 0 for m > dim X for every constructible sheaf F (SGA 4 XIV 3.2).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
f affine; for Rf_!, f separated of finite type and Λ a finite ring (reduced to self-injective ℤ/ℓ^a-coefficients by restriction of scalars).
For the cohomology statements k is separably closed (BBD state 4.1.4–4.1.5 for k algebraically closed; the purely inseparable extension k̄/k changes no étale cohomology, by topological invariance).
proofSteps: Right t-exactness of Rf_*: a constructible K lies in pD^{≤d} iff each ℋ^m(K)[−m] does, so it suffices that dim Supp R^qf_*F ≤ dim Supp F − q for every constructible F on X: Artin's affine theorem SGA 4 XIV 3.1, requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (BBD 4.1.1, p.102–103).

Left t-exactness of Rf_!: Verdier duality D Rf_* ≅ Rf_! D (EDC.1:biduality/duality-exchange-isomorphisms) with EDC.5/perverse-verdier-self-duality (BBD 4.1.2) for self-injective Λ; for a finite ring Λ killed by n, restriction of scalars to ℤ/n = ∏ ℤ/ℓ^a keeps constructibility, commutes with Rf_!, stalks and costalks (EDC.0/coefficient-change) and detects both aisles (BBD 4.0), and each ℤ/ℓ^a is self-injective.

Quasi-finite affine f: EDC.5/quasi-finite-perverse-exactness supplies the other half (BBD 4.1.3; its proof cites 4.1.7 for the right t-exactness of f_*, meaning 4.1.1: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves/E16).
Cohomology: apply 4.1.1 to Z → Spec k after the quasi-finite pullback u^*K ∈ pD^{≤0}(Z) (BBD 4.1.5); H_c by duality over a separably closed field.
acceptance: For X = 𝔸¹ over k̄ and K = Λ[1]: H^m(𝔸¹, Λ[1]) = 0 for m > 0 (H¹(𝔸¹, Λ) = 0), and H^m_c(𝔸¹, Λ[1]) = 0 for m < 0 (H⁰_c(𝔸¹, Λ) = 0).
Non-example (affineness): for P¹ over k̄ and K = Λ[1], H¹(P¹, Λ[1]) = H²(P¹, Λ) ≅ Λ(−1) ≠ 0.
For X = 𝔾_m over k̄, H¹(𝔾_m, Λ) ≅ Λ(−1) ≠ 0 in degree 1 = dim X: the bound m > dim X is sharp.

sources.match: For f affine Rf_* is right t-exact (a reformulation of SGA 4 XIV 3.1) and Rf_! left t-exact; quasi-finite affine f gives t-exact f_! and f_*; over an algebraically closed field the cohomology of an affine variety vanishes above its dimension, and K ∈ pD^{≤0} has no positive cohomology on affine quasi-finite Z.

nodes.title: Affine open immersions: exactness and the four-term sequences
nodes.statement: Let j : U → X be an affine open immersion (for example the complement of an effective Cartier divisor) with closed complement i : D → X. Then: (i) for a perverse G on U, j_!G and Rj_*G are perverse; (ii) for a perverse F on X, i^*F ∈ pD^{[−1,0]}(D) and i^!F ∈ pD^{[0,1]}(D), and there are exact sequences of perverse sheaves 0 → i_*pH^{−1}i^*F → j_!j^*F → F → i_*pH⁰i^*F → 0 and 0 → i_*pH⁰i^!F → F → Rj_*j^*F → i_*pH¹i^!F → 0; (iii) for a perverse G on U there is an exact sequence 0 → i_*pH^{−1}(i^*Rj_*G) → j_!G → Rj_*G → i_*pH⁰(i^*Rj_*G) → 0, and i^*j_!*G[−1] and i^!j_!*G[1] are perverse with i^*j_!*G[−1] ≅ pH^{−1}(i^*Rj_*G) ≅ pH⁰(i^!j_!G) and i^!j_!*G[1] ≅ pH⁰(i^*Rj_*G) ≅ pH¹(i^!j_!G) (BBD 4.1.10–4.1.12).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
j an affine open immersion; Λ self-injective where the left t-exactness of j_! is deduced by duality.
proofSteps: (i) is EDC.5/perverse-artin-vanishing for the quasi-finite affine j (BBD 4.1.3).
(ii): the perverse cohomology sequences of the triangles j_!j^*F → F → i_*i^*F and i_*i^!F → F → Rj_*j^*F, with j_!j^*F and Rj_*j^*F perverse by (i), force the stated amplitudes (BBD 4.1.10).

(iii): (ii) for F = Rj_*G gives the sequence (BBD (4.1.11.1)); comparing with (ii) for F = j_!G through i^*Rj_*G ≅ i^!j_!G[1] identifies the end terms, and j_!*G is the image of j_!G → Rj_*G (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension), whence the descriptions of i^*j_!*G[−1] and i^!j_!*G[1] (BBD 4.1.12).
acceptance: For j : 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ over k̄ and G = Λ[1]: pH^{−1}(i^*Rj_*G) ≅ Λ_0 and pH⁰(i^*Rj_*G) ≅ Λ_0(−1), the sequence 0 → i_*Λ_0 → j_!Λ[1] → Rj_*Λ[1] → i_*Λ_0(−1) → 0 is exact, j_!*G ≅ Λ_{𝔸¹}[1], i^*j_!*G[−1] ≅ Λ_0 and i^!j_!*G[1] ≅ Λ_0(−1).

Non-example: for the non-affine complement j of a closed point x in a smooth surface S, Rj_*Λ[2] is not perverse: R³j_*Λ ≠ 0 at x (from H⁴_x(S, Λ) ≅ Λ(−2)), giving cohomology in degree 1 at a point of dimension 0.

sources.match: For an affine open immersion j with closed complement, j_! and j_* preserve perversity, i^*F and i^!F have perverse amplitude [−1,0] and [0,1] with four-term exact sequences, and i^*j_!*G[−1], i^!j_!*G[1] are perverse and computed by perverse cohomology of i^*j_*G and i^!j_!G.

nodes.title: External tensor product is t-exact
nodes.statement: For X₁, X₂ separated of finite type over k and Λ a field (finite of characteristic ℓ, or E under the ℓ-adic hypotheses), the external tensor product K ⊠ L := pr₁^*K ⊗ pr₂^*L : D^b_c(X₁, Λ) × D^b_c(X₂, Λ) → D^b_c(X₁ ×_k X₂, Λ) is t-exact in each variable for the middle perverse t-structures; in particular the external product of perverse sheaves is perverse and IC_{X₁}(L₁) ⊠ IC_{X₂}(L₂) ≅ IC_{X₁×X₂}(L₁ ⊠ L₂). It commutes with Rf_*, Rf_!, f^*, f^! for products of morphisms and with Verdier duality (BBD 4.2.7).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ a field; the statement is false for ℤ_ℓ or ℤ/ℓ² coefficients without flatness, since ⊗ is not exact (BBD 4.0 (d)).
proofSteps: Künneth formulas for ⊠ with the six operations, and D(K ⊠ L) ≅ DK ⊠ DL: imported (SGA 4 XVII 5.4.3, through SF.2 as requested by EDC.0) and BBD 4.2.7.

Choose stratifications T₁, T₂ adapted to K and L (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure stratum criterion); on S₁ × S₂, i^*(K ⊠ L) = i^*K ⊠ i^*L and i^!(K ⊠ L) = i^!K ⊠ i^!L, and the cutoff −dim(S₁ × S₂) = −dim S₁ − dim S₂ is additive; over a field, ℋ of a tensor product of complexes with lisse cohomology is the tensor product of cohomologies (BBD 4.2.8, which stresses the linearity of the perversity function).
IC: the external product of j_!* is j_!* of the external product by the strict support conditions and EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension.
acceptance: Λ_{C₁}[1] ⊠ Λ_{C₂}[1] ≅ Λ_{C₁×C₂}[2] for smooth curves C₁, C₂.
For Λ = ℤ/ℓ²: (ℤ/ℓ)_{pt} ⊠ (ℤ/ℓ)_{pt} = ℤ/ℓ ⊗^L ℤ/ℓ has cohomology in degrees −1 and 0, so it is not perverse.

sources.locator: 4.2.7, pp.111–112; Proposition 4.2.8 and its proof, p.112
sources.match: The external tensor product commutes with the usual operations and with duality; for a field of coefficients it is t-exact, checked stratum by stratum on product stratifications, the perversity being linear in dimension.

nodes.title: Intermediate extension of perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let j : U → X be a locally closed immersion of separated schemes of finite type over k, factored as an open immersion j′ : U → Ū into its closure followed by the closed immersion ī : Ū → X, and put Z := Ū ∖ U. The intermediate extension is j_!* := ī_* ∘ j′_!* : Perv(U, Λ) → Perv(X, Λ), where j′_!*A is the image of pH⁰(j′_!A) → pH⁰(Rj′_*A) (EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension for the perverse recollement of EDC.5/open-closed-perverse-recollement). For A perverse on U, j′_!*A is the unique perverse sheaf P on Ū with P|_U ≅ A, ℋ^m(i_x^*P) = 0 for m ≥ −dim(x) and ℋ^m(i_x^!P) = 0 for m ≤ −dim(x) at every point x of Z (BBD 2.1.9 in the pointwise form of 2.2.12); equivalently the unique perverse extension with no nonzero perverse subobject or quotient supported on Z. It is fully faithful, sends simple objects to simple objects, is independent of the factorisation, and is transitive: (j₂ ∘ j₁)_!* ≅ j₂_!* ∘ j₁_!* (BBD (2.1.7.1)). If i : Z → Ū is the closed complement, i^*j′_!*A ∈ pD^{≤−1}(Z) and i^!j′_!*A ∈ pD^{≥1}(Z).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
j a locally closed immersion; A perverse on U.
proofSteps: Open dense case: EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension applied to the glued perverse t-structure (EDC.5/open-closed-perverse-recollement), giving image, characterisations, full faithfulness and simplicity.

Pointwise strict bounds: the conditions i^*P ∈ pD^{≤−1}(Z), i^!P ∈ pD^{≥1}(Z) of BBD 1.4.24 translate through the pointwise description of the perverse t-structure of Z (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure; dim(x) is the same in Z and in X) into the strict stalk and costalk vanishing (BBD 2.1.9).
Transitivity (BBD (2.1.7.1)): apply pj_!, pj_!*, pj_* to the maps pk_! → pk_!* → pk_* and compose; independence of the factorisation follows from the characterisation.
Closed pushforward ī_* is t-exact and fully faithful on perverse sheaves (EDC.5/quasi-finite-perverse-exactness).
acceptance: For j : 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ over k̄ and L a nontrivial rank-one Kummer local system, j_!L[1] ≅ j_!*(L[1]) ≅ Rj_*L[1].
For j : 𝔾_m → 𝔸¹ and Λ[1], j_!*(Λ[1]) ≅ Λ_{𝔸¹}[1], while j_!(Λ[1]) and Rj_*(Λ[1]) are different perverse sheaves.

nodes.title: Deligne's truncation formula for the intermediate extension
nodes.statement: Let j : U → X be an open immersion whose closed complement F is smooth over k (after passing to k^perf) of pure dimension d, and A perverse on U. If ℋ^m(Rj_*A)|_F is locally constant for every m ≥ −d, then j_!*A ≅ τ_{≤−d−1}Rj_*A for the natural truncation (BBD 2.2.4.1); if the local constancy holds for m ≥ −d − 1 (resp. m ≥ −d + 1) then pH⁰(j_!A) ≅ τ_{≤−d−2}Rj_*A (resp. pH⁰(Rj_*A) ≅ τ_{≤−d}Rj_*A). More generally, for a filtration X = U_N ⊃ … ⊃ U_k = U by opens such that each U_{m+1} ∖ U_m is smooth of pure dimension −m − 1 and the hypothesis holds at each step, j_!*A ≅ τ_{≤ N−1}Rj_{N*} ∘ … ∘ τ_{≤ k}Rj_{k+1,*}A, with j_{m+1} : U_m → U_{m+1} (BBD 2.1.11).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
The local constancy hypothesis on ℋ^m(Rj_*A)|_F is part of the statement; it fails in general (wild ramification), and without it the natural truncation does not compute j_!* in the étale setting.
proofSteps: By EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension (b) (BBD 1.4.23), j_!*A ≅ τ^F_{≤−1}Rj_*A for the perverse truncation relative to F (BBD (2.2.3.1)).

On F, smooth of pure dimension d, complexes with locally constant cohomology sheaves have the perverse t-structure equal to the natural one shifted by d (EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse), so for the part of Rj_*A in degrees ≥ −d the relative perverse truncation is τ_{≤−d−1} (BBD 2.2.4 with the stratum criterion 2.2.2 (iii)).
Iterate along the filtration using transitivity (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension), as in BBD 2.1.11.
acceptance: For a smooth curve C, an open dense j : U → C and L locally constant on U (the hypothesis holds at the finitely many points of F), j_!*(L[1]) ≅ (j_*L)[1] with j_* the underived direct image.

sources.match: For F smooth of dimension d with ℋ^ij_*A locally constant on F for i ≥ p(2d) = −d, j_!*A is the natural truncation τ_{≤−d−1}j_*A; similar formulas for pj_! and pj_* under the shifted hypotheses.
For a perversity decreasing under specialization, j_!*A is the iterated composite of direct images and natural truncations along the filtration by unions of strata of bounded perversity.

nodes.title: Low-degree cohomology of an intermediate extension across a boundary of high codimension
nodes.statement: Let j : U → X be an open immersion whose closed complement Z has codimension ≥ c in every component (dim Z ≤ d − c with X of pure dimension d), A perverse on U and P := j_!*A. Then the cone C of the natural map P → Rj_*A lies in i_*pD^{≥0}(Z) ⊆ i_*D^{≥ −dim Z}, hence in the natural D^{≥ c−d}; consequently, for every étale V → X, H^m(V, P) → H^m(V ∩ U, A) is an isomorphism for m ≤ c − d − 1 and injective for m = c − d. For A = L[d] with L a sheaf on U: H^q(X, P[−d]) ≅ H^q(U, L) for q ≤ c − 1 and H^c(X, P[−d]) → H^c(U, L) is injective. In particular, for X̄ smooth of pure dimension d, D ⊂ X̄ a strict normal crossings divisor with singular locus D_sing (codimension ≥ 2), X := X̄ ∖ D, a : X → U := X̄ ∖ D_sing, b : U → X̄ and F locally constant on X such that the ℋ^mRa_*F are locally constant along D ∖ D_sing, one has b_!*((a_*F)[d]) = j_!*(F[d]) and H¹(X̄, j_!*(F[d])[−d]) ≅ H¹(U, a_*F).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
codim (X ∖ U) ≥ c in each component of X, X of pure dimension d.
proofSteps: The recollement triangle i_*i^!P → P → Rj_*j^*P gives C ≅ i_*i^!P[1]; i^!P ∈ pD^{≥1}(Z) by the strict costalk bound (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension), so C ∈ i_*pD^{≥0}(Z).
pD^{≥0}(Z) ⊆ D^{≥−dim Z} (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure bounds), and −dim Z ≥ c − d.
Long exact cohomology sequence of P → Rj_*A → C on V.

SNC case: a_!*(F[d]) = (a_*F)[d] by EDC.5/deligne-truncation-formula (D ∖ D_sing is smooth of dimension d − 1, under the stated local constancy), transitivity gives j_!* = b_!* a_!*, and the codimension-two case of the first part applied to b gives the H¹ isomorphism.
acceptance: For X = 𝔸², U = 𝔸² ∖ {0}, A = Λ[2]: P = Λ_{𝔸²}[2], and H^q(𝔸², Λ) → H^q(U, Λ) is an isomorphism for q ≤ 1 and injective for q = 2 (here c = 2), while H³(U, Λ) ≅ Λ(−2) ≠ 0 = H³(𝔸², Λ).

For the nodal cubic X with node s, normalisation ν : P¹ → X and U = X ∖ {s} (c = 1, d = 1): IC_X[−1] = ν_*Λ, so H⁰(X, IC_X[−1]) = H⁰(P¹, Λ) ≅ Λ ≅ H⁰(U, Λ) (degree c − 1), and H¹(X, IC_X[−1]) = H¹(P¹, Λ) = 0 injects into H¹(U, Λ) ≅ Λ(−1) (degree c).

nodes.title: The intersection complex of a local system
nodes.statement: Let X be a separated scheme of finite type over k, irreducible of dimension d, U ⊂ X a dense open subscheme smooth over k (one exists when k is perfect; in general pass to k^perf by EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure), j : U → X the inclusion and L a locally constant constructible sheaf of Λ-modules on U. The intersection complex is IC_X(L) := j_!*(L[d]) ∈ Perv(X, Λ) (EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension, EDC.5/shifted-local-systems-perverse), and IC_X := IC_X(Λ). It does not depend on U: for U′ ⊂ U dense open, IC_X(L) ≅ IC_X(L|_{U′}). Its restriction to U is L[d] (no Tate twist and no shift by 2d). If X is smooth, IC_X(L) = L[d]; if dim X = 1, IC_X(L) ≅ (j_*L)[1]; if ν : X′ → X is finite and an isomorphism over U with X′ smooth of pure dimension d and L′ locally constant on X′ extending L, then IC_X(L) ≅ ν_*(L′[d]); IC_X(L) is simple if L is irreducible and Λ is a field. No half-twist normalisation is built into the definition.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ is a noetherian commutative ring with nΛ = 0; D^b_c(X, Λ) is the bounded constructible category of EDC.0/constructible-ctf-complexes.
X irreducible of dimension d; U dense open and smooth over k; L locally constant constructible on U.
proofSteps: Definition through EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension applied to the perverse sheaf L[d] on U.

Independence of U: transitivity (j_U ∘ j′)_!* = j_{U!*} ∘ j′_!* and j′_!*(L|_{U′}[d]) = L[d] because a shifted local system on smooth U satisfies the strict boundary bounds on U ∖ U′ by purity (BBD Lemme 4.3.2).
Curves: EDC.5/deligne-truncation-formula with a zero-dimensional boundary.

Finite birational ν: ν_* is t-exact (EDC.5/quasi-finite-perverse-exactness) and finite fibres over the boundary give the strict stalk and costalk bounds (proper base change for finite maps), so ν_*(L′[d]) is the unique extension.
Simplicity for irreducible L over a field: EDC.5/simple-perverse-sheaves-classification (BBD 4.3.3).
acceptance: IC of a smooth curve is Λ[1]; IC of a nodal cubic is ν_*Λ_{P¹}[1], whose stalk at the node is Λ² in degree −1.
IC of a cuspidal cubic X is Λ_X[1], since its normalisation is a universal homeomorphism.

nodes.title: Finite length and the simple perverse sheaves
nodes.statement: Let Λ be a field (finite of characteristic ℓ ≠ char k, or E/ℚ_ℓ finite under the ℓ-adic hypotheses, or its algebraic closure). Every perverse sheaf on X has finite length in Perv(X, Λ): the category is artinian and noetherian. The simple perverse sheaves are exactly the objects i_{V̄*}IC_{V̄}(L) = j_{V!*}(L[dim V]), where j_V : V → X is the inclusion of an irreducible locally closed subscheme smooth over k (after passage to k^perf) and L is an irreducible locally constant sheaf of Λ-modules on V; two such are isomorphic iff the closures of the V agree and the L agree on a common dense open. For Λ = O/λ^m every perverse sheaf has finite length (its simple constituents are those of the λ-adic graded pieces, which are O/λ-perverse); for Λ = O the category is only noetherian and its dual p⁺-category only artinian.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ a field for the classification; X separated of finite type over k.
proofSteps: Reduce to k perfect by topological invariance (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure).

Simplicity of L[dim V] on smooth irreducible V for irreducible L: a perverse subobject is M[dim V] on a dense open for a lisse subsheaf M; irreducibility persists on dense opens because π₁(U) → π₁(V) is surjective for V normal irreducible (Stacks Tag 0BQI, requested from SF.2); then the no-sub/quotient characterisation of j_!* (BBD 4.3.3, citing 1.4.25: EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves/E17).
Simplicity of i_{V̄*}j_!*: twice EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension (d) (BBD 4.3.4).

Finite length by noetherian induction: a perverse F is L[dim U] on a smooth irreducible dense open U of its support with L lisse of finite length, so the four-term sequences of EDC.5/open-closed-perverse-recollement reduce to intermediate extensions of the constituents of L and to perverse sheaves on smaller supports (BBD 4.3.4); the classification is EDC.5/recollement-intermediate-extension (e).
O/λ^m: filter by λ^iF; O: BBD 4.0 (b) and Juteau §1.1.

Over Λ = ℤ_ℓ on a point, ℤ_ℓ has the infinite descending chain ℤ_ℓ ⊃ ℓℤ_ℓ ⊃ …, so Perv(pt, ℤ_ℓ) is not artinian.

nodes.title: Perverse t-structures with ℓ-adic coefficients
nodes.statement: Assume the ℓ-adic hypotheses: E/ℚ_ℓ finite with ring of integers O and uniformizer λ, and k with finite H^i(Gal(k^sep/k′), ℤ/ℓ) for all finite k′/k. On the ℓ-adic constructible categories D^b_c(X, O) (constructible complexes of finite Tor-dimension at each level λ^m, as a 2-limit) and D^b_c(X, E) := D^b_c(X, O) ⊗_O E, the middle perverse t-structures are defined by the stalk and costalk conditions (4.0.1)–(4.0.2) on the cohomology sheaves ℋ^m (constructible O- and E-sheaves), equivalently by gluing as in EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure. Then: K ∈ pD^{≤0}(X, O) iff K ⊗^L_O O/λ ∈ pD^{≤0}(X, O/λ) (BBD 2.2.17); for every interval [a, b] the functor pD^{[a,b]}(X, O) ⊗ E → pD^{[a,b]}(X, E) is an equivalence, so Perv(X, E) = Perv(X, O) ⊗_O E (BBD 2.2.18); the results of EDC.5 stated for torsion coefficients (recollement, intermediate extension, quasi-finite, affine, smooth and fibre-dimension exactness) hold for O and E coefficients (BBD 2.2.19, 4.0); for E the perverse t-structure is self-dual (EDC.5/perverse-verdier-self-duality), for O it is not (EDC.5/integral-dual-perversity).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).

For ℓ-adic coefficients (E/ℚ_ℓ finite, ring of integers O, uniformizer λ, ℓ ≠ char k) the base field satisfies BBD's finiteness condition: H^i(Gal(k^sep/k′), ℤ/ℓ) is finite for every finite k′/k and every i (BBD 2.2.14 and 4.0; for example k finite or separably closed). The categories D^b_c(X, O) and D^b_c(X, E) and their operations are the ℓ-adic formalism requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.
Pro-étale constructible categories (Bhatt–Scholze) remove the Galois-finiteness condition; they are a different supplied category, not used here.
proofSteps: The categories and their operations, compatible with reduction modulo λ^m, are the ℓ-adic formalism requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 (BBD 2.2.14–2.2.16 after Deligne's Weil II 1.1.2; 2-limits of triangulated categories with finite Hom sets are triangulated, BBD 2.2.15).
Upper aisle via reduction: the exact sequences 0 → ℋ^mK ⊗ ℤ/ℓ^n → ℋ^m(K ⊗ ℤ/ℓ^n) → Tor(ℋ^{m+1}K, ℤ/ℓ^n) → 0 (2.2.16.1) show that the support conditions on K and on K ⊗^L O/λ agree (BBD 2.2.17).
Gluing along (S, L)-constructible subcategories and passage to the limit over (S, L) as in EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure (BBD 2.2.17–2.2.18); the equivalence after ⊗ E from Hom-finiteness.
The torsion-coefficient theorems transfer by the conservativity of reduction modulo λ and of restriction of scalars (BBD 4.0).
acceptance: For X = Spec Ω, Ω separably closed: Perv(X, O) is finitely generated O-modules in degree 0 and Perv(X, E) is finite-dimensional E-vector spaces.
On a smooth curve C, O_C[1] and E_C[1] are perverse; (O/λ)_C[1] ∈ D^b_c(C, O) is p-perverse.

nodes.title: The dual integral perversity p⁺ and its exchange with p
nodes.statement: Under the ℓ-adic hypotheses, let p be the middle perverse t-structure on D^b_c(X, O) (EDC.5/adic-perverse-t-structures). Its heart Perv(X, O) is O-linear and noetherian, so (λ-power torsion, λ-torsion-free) is a torsion theory on it, and p⁺ is the tilt (EDC.5/torsion-pair-tilt): p⁺D^{≤0} = {K ∈ pD^{≤1} : pH¹K is torsion} and p⁺D^{≥0} = {K ∈ pD^{≥0} : pH⁰K is torsion-free}. Pointwise, K ∈ p⁺D^{≤0} iff ℋ^m(i_x^*K) = 0 for m > −dim(x) + 1 and ℋ^{−dim(x)+1}(i_x^*K) is torsion at every point x, and K ∈ p⁺D^{≥0} iff ℋ^m(i_x^!K) = 0 for m < −dim(x) and ℋ^{−dim(x)}(i_x^!K) is torsion-free. Then pD^{≤0} ⊆ p⁺D^{≤0} ⊆ pD^{≤1}; Verdier duality on D^b_c(X, O) exchanges p and p⁺: D(pD^{≤0}) = p⁺D^{≥0} and D(pD^{≥0}) = p⁺D^{≤0}, so D maps Perv(X, O)^op onto the p⁺-heart and not onto itself; a p-perverse K is p⁺-perverse iff it is torsion-free in Perv(X, O); an exact functor is right t-exact for p iff it is for p⁺; K ↦ K ⊗ E is t-exact from both p and p⁺; the p⁺-heart is artinian while Perv(X, O) is noetherian.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).

For ℓ-adic coefficients (E/ℚ_ℓ finite, ring of integers O, uniformizer λ, ℓ ≠ char k) the base field satisfies BBD's finiteness condition: H^i(Gal(k^sep/k′), ℤ/ℓ) is finite for every finite k′/k and every i (BBD 2.2.14 and 4.0; for example k finite or separably closed). The categories D^b_c(X, O) and D^b_c(X, E) and their operations are the ℓ-adic formalism requested from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2.
O-linear noetherian heart: torsion means killed by some λ^N, torsion-free means λ is a monomorphism.
proofSteps: The torsion theory on the noetherian O-linear heart: Juteau Props. 1.3.4–1.3.5; the tilt: EDC.5/torsion-pair-tilt.
Pointwise description: BBD 3.3.4 (i)–(iv) in the stratified setting, passed to the limit over stratifications (BBD 3.3.5), giving Juteau's (1.4)–(1.9).

Duality: on a smooth stratum, RHom_O(−, O) on lisse O-sheaves exchanges the natural t-structure with its tilt, shifted by the dimension, because Ext¹_O(T, O) is torsion in degree 1 for torsion T (BBD 3.3.1, 3.3.3); glue with the ℓ-adic exchange formulas D i^* ≅ i^! D (requested from SF.2 with the ℓ-adic formalism) as in BBD 3.3.4 (p.100).
Exactness statements: BBD 3.3.4 (the right t-exact criterion) and the tilt inclusions; rationalisation kills torsion.

On a smooth curve C, D_C(O_C[1]) ≅ O_C(1)[1] is in both hearts, but D_C((O/λ)_C[1]) ≅ (O/λ)_C(1)[0] is p⁺-perverse and not p-perverse.

nodes.title: Perversity conditions on nonconstructible complexes
nodes.statement: Let X be separated of finite type over k and Λ torsion (nΛ = 0, n invertible in k). For a ∈ ℤ and K in the unbounded derived category D(X, Λ) (EDC.0/etale-derived-category), say K ∈ pD^{≤a}_{ext}(X, Λ) if ℋ^m(i_x^*K) = 0 for m > a − dim(x) at every point x, and K ∈ pD^{≥a}_{ext}(X, Λ) if K is bounded below and ℋ^m(i_x^!K) = 0 for m < a − dim(x) at every point x (i_x^! := restriction of i^! along {x}^− → X to x, EDC.1:adjoint/local-cohomology-identification). Then: (a) on D^b_c(X, Λ) these are the aisles of the middle perverse t-structure; (b) pD^{≤a}_{ext} is closed under extensions, arbitrary direct sums and filtered colimits; (c) pD^{≥a}_{ext} is closed under extensions and under filtered colimits of systems that are uniformly bounded below (all K_α ∈ D^{≥b} for one b), because for such systems geometric costalks commute with the colimit; (d) for j : U → X open, Rj_* preserves pD^{≥a}_{ext} and j^* preserves both conditions; for f : X → Y finite, f_* preserves both; for u étale, u^* preserves both and detects them when surjective. No t-structure on D(X, Λ) and no constructibility of filtered colimits is asserted.
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).
Λ torsion with nΛ = 0; X noetherian (separated of finite type over k); the lower condition includes bounded-belowness so that the costalk of a filtered colimit is computed by the colimit of costalks.
proofSteps: (a): definitions agree with (4.0.1)–(4.0.2) (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure).
(b): stalks are exact and commute with all colimits.

(c): ℋ^m(i_x^!K) is the colimit over étale neighbourhoods V of x and closed W = {x}^− ∩ V of H^m_W(V, K); with a uniform lower bound b, H^m_W(V, −) depends only on τ_{≤m+1}, a bounded complex in [b, m+1], and étale cohomology with supports of the qcqs V commutes with filtered colimits of sheaves (SF.2/cohomology-filtered-colimits via the localization triangle of EDC.0/cohomology-with-supports); induct on the length.

(d): for x ∉ U, {x}^− ⊆ X ∖ U and i^!Rj_* = 0 (EDC.5/recollement-situation), so the costalk of Rj_*K at x vanishes; for x ∈ U it is that of K. Finite f: f_* is exact, stalks of f_*K at y are the sums of stalks over the finitely many points above y, and i_y^!f_*K = f′_*i′^!K by base change for the closed immersion; dim is preserved by quasi-finite maps (EDC.5/point-dimension-function). Étale u: stalks and costalks are preserved.
acceptance: A filtered colimit of perverse sheaves Λ_C[1] → … along the identity is Λ_C[1].
For a smooth curve C and the direct sum K = ⊕_{x ∈ C closed} i_{x*}Λ[0] (not constructible), K ∈ pD^{≤0}_{ext} ∩ pD^{≥0}_{ext}.

nodes.title: Proper semismall pushforward preserves perversity
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper morphism of separated schemes of finite type over k and Λ self-injective (a finite field of characteristic ℓ, O/λ^m, ℤ/ℓ^m) or E under the ℓ-adic hypotheses. Let X = ⊔_α X_α be a finite partition into locally closed equidimensional strata and Y = ⊔_β Y_β a finite partition into locally closed subsets, such that for all α, β and every geometric point ȳ of Y_β: 2·dim(f^{−1}(ȳ) ∩ X_α) + dim Y_β ≤ dim X_α (with dim ∅ = −∞). Let K be a perverse sheaf on X such that the cohomology sheaves of i_α^*K and of i_α^*D_X K are locally constant on each X_α. Then Rf_*K = Rf_!K is perverse. In particular (one stratum): if X is smooth of pure dimension n, L is locally constant on X and dim(X ×_Y X) ≤ n — equivalently 2·dim f^{−1}(ȳ) + dim Y_β ≤ n for a partition of Y — then Rf_*(L[n]) is perverse (f is semismall).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).

For duality statements Λ is moreover self-injective (a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ char k, or O_E/λ^m, or ℤ/ℓ^m; EDC.1:biduality/self-injective-coefficients), the setting of EDC.1:biduality/constructible-biduality.
f proper; the strata hypotheses as stated; no local triviality of f over the Y_β is needed.
Self-injective coefficients are needed for the cosupport half, which is deduced from the support half by duality; for O = ℤ_ℓ duality exchanges p and p⁺ and the statement is not asserted here.
proofSteps: Support: for ȳ in Y_β, (Rf_*K)_ȳ ≅ RΓ(f^{−1}(ȳ), K) by proper base change (imported through SF.2), and RΓ(f^{−1}(ȳ), K) = RΓ_c because the fibre is proper. Filter the fibre by the locally closed pieces Z_α := f^{−1}(ȳ) ∩ X_α (compact-support localization sequences, EDC.0/compact-pushforward-amplitude-and-colimits).

On X_α the cohomology sheaves of K are locally constant, so the stalk condition at the generic points of X_α gives ℋ^m(K|_{X_α}) = 0 for m > −dim X_α everywhere on X_α (EDC.5/middle-perverse-t-structure). Since H^q_c(Z, F) = 0 for q > 2·dim Z and every torsion sheaf F (EDC.2:trace-purity/top-degree-compact-cohomology), the hypercohomology spectral sequence gives H^m_c(Z_α, K) = 0 for m > 2·dim Z_α − dim X_α ≤ −dim Y_β. Hence ℋ^m(Rf_*K)_ȳ = 0 for m > −dim Y_β ≥ −dim(y), which is (4.0.1) at y; so Rf_*K ∈ pD^{≤0}(Y).

Cosupport: D_X K is perverse (EDC.5/perverse-verdier-self-duality) and satisfies the same stratum hypotheses, so Rf_*D_X K ∈ pD^{≤0}(Y); D_Y Rf_*K ≅ Rf_!D_X K = Rf_*D_X K (EDC.1:adjoint/formal-duality-exchange, f proper), hence Rf_*K ∈ pD^{≥0}(Y) by self-duality.

Smooth source: take one stratum X; K = L[n] and D_X K = L^∨(n)[n] have locally constant cohomology; dim(X ×_Y X) ≤ n is the stated inequality summed over the strata of a partition of Y by fibre dimension (de Cataldo–Migliorini Prop. 4.2.1, there over ℂ with a topologically locally trivial stratification, which this étale argument does not need).
acceptance: A proper surjective generically finite map of smooth surfaces is semismall (fibres of dimension ≤ 1 over finitely many points), so Rf_*Λ[2] is perverse; e.g. the blow-up of a point of 𝔸².

Non-example: the blow-up f of a point in 𝔸³ (exceptional divisor P² over the point, 2·2 + 0 > 3) is not semismall, and Rf_*Λ[3] has stalk H⁴(P², Λ) ≠ 0 in degree 1 at the point, so it is not perverse.

nodes.title: Small maps push intersection complexes to intersection complexes
nodes.statement: Let f : X → Y be a proper surjective morphism of irreducible separated schemes of finite type over k, X smooth of pure dimension n, Λ self-injective (or E), L locally constant on X, and suppose f is small: there is a partition Y = ⊔ Y_β into locally closed subsets with a dense open stratum Y_0 such that 2·dim f^{−1}(ȳ) + dim Y_β < n for every β ≠ 0 and ȳ ∈ Y_β. Assume moreover that f is finite étale over a dense open V ⊂ Y_0 smooth over k (generic étaleness is a hypothesis: smallness does not imply it in characteristic p). Then dim Y = n and Rf_*(L[n]) ≅ IC_Y((f_*L)|_V).
hypotheses: k is a field, n ≥ 1 an integer invertible in k, and X, Y, Z, U are separated schemes of finite type over k; every point x has dim(x) := dim of its closure (EDC.5/point-dimension-function).

For duality statements Λ is moreover self-injective (a finite field of characteristic ℓ ≠ char k, or O_E/λ^m, or ℤ/ℓ^m; EDC.1:biduality/self-injective-coefficients), the setting of EDC.1:biduality/constructible-biduality.
f proper surjective, X smooth of pure dimension n, f small, f finite étale over a dense smooth open V.
proofSteps: Rf_*(L[n]) is perverse by EDC.5/semismall-pushforward-perversity (small implies semismall).

Strict support: for ȳ ∉ V in Y_β of dimension b, the support computation of the semismall proof gives ℋ^m(Rf_*L[n])_ȳ = 0 for m > 2·dim f^{−1}(ȳ) − n, and smallness makes this < −b, including the zero-dimensional fibres over strata with b < n (where −n < −b). Strict cosupport by duality: D_Y Rf_*(L[n]) ≅ Rf_*(L^∨(n)[n]).
These are the strict bounds of EDC.5/perverse-intermediate-extension along Y ∖ V, so Rf_*(L[n]) ≅ j_!*((Rf_*L[n])|_V) = IC_Y((f_*L)|_V) (EDC.5/intersection-complex-of-local-system).
acceptance: The normalisation ν of a nodal cubic is small (over the node the fibre is two points: 2·0 + 0 < 1) and finite étale over the smooth locus, so ν_*Λ_{P¹}[1] = IC_X.

Non-example: the blow-up f of a point in 𝔸² is semismall but not small (2·1 + 0 = 2): the stalk of Rf_*Λ[2] at the origin is H^*(P¹, Λ)[2], with ℋ⁰ ≅ H²(P¹, Λ) ≅ Λ(−1) ≠ 0 at a point of dimension 0, which the strict stalk bound of an intersection complex forbids; so Rf_*Λ[2] is perverse but is not IC_{𝔸²}.

sources.match: If dim S_k + 2d_k < dim X for every non-dense stratum the map is small and f_*ℚ_X[n] satisfies the support and cosupport conditions of intersection cohomology, so it is IC_Y of the local system on the open set where f is a covering.

requests.need: Artin's affine theorem in the form BBD 4.1.1 uses (SGA 4 XIV 3.1–3.2): for f : X → Y an affine morphism of schemes of finite type over a field k, n invertible in k, Λ noetherian with nΛ = 0 and F a constructible sheaf of Λ-modules on X, dim Supp R^qf_*F ≤ dim Supp F − q for every q (dim computed with dim(x) = dim of the closure of x); in particular, for X affine over a separably closed field, H^q(X, F) = 0 for q > dim X.

Topological invariance of the étale site (Stacks Tag 04DY, Section 59.45): a universal homeomorphism, in particular X_{k^perf} → X for X of finite type over a field k, induces an equivalence of small étale sites, hence of D(−, Λ), compatible with pullback and pushforward, stalks at geometric points, constructibility, Rf_!, f^! and the closed/open recollement.

Étale fundamental groups of geometrically unibranch schemes (Stacks Tag 0BQI): for X irreducible and geometrically unibranch (e.g. normal, e.g. smooth over k) and U ⊂ X nonempty open, π₁(U, ū) → π₁(X, ū) is surjective; consequently restriction from X to U is fully faithful on locally constant constructible sheaves and preserves irreducibility.

The ℓ-adic constructible formalism (EllAdicRealization of CohomologicalPointCounting; Deligne, Weil II 1.1.2–1.1.3; BBD 2.2.14–2.2.18): for k with finite H^i(Gal(k^sep/k′), ℤ/ℓ) for all finite k′/k, ℓ ≠ char k, E/ℚ_ℓ finite with integers O and uniformizer λ: the triangulated categories D^b_c(X, O) (2-limit of D^b_ctf(X, O/λ^m) along − ⊗^L O/λ^m) and D^b_c(X, E) = D^b_c(X, O) ⊗ E, their natural t-structures with hearts the constructible O- and E-sheaves, the six operations f^*, Rf_*, Rf_!, f^!, ⊗^L, RHom with Verdier duality D_X = RHom(−, a^!O), biduality, the exchange formulas D i^* ≅ i^! D and D Rf_* ≅ Rf_! D on constructible complexes, and compatibility of all of these with reduction modulo λ^m and with ⊗_O E.

Base change and finiteness inputs already requested by EDC.0 from CohomologicalPointCounting, in the forms EDC.5 uses: proper base change (Rf_*K)_ȳ ≅ RΓ(f^{−1}(ȳ), K) for f proper and torsion K; exactness of finite pushforward with stalks the sum over the finite fibre; smooth base change and f^*RHom(K, L) ≅ RHom(f^*K, f^*L) for f smooth and K constructible; the finiteness theorem (Rf_*, Rj_* and i^! preserve D^b_c(−, Λ) for Λ noetherian with nΛ = 0, SGA 4½ [Th. finitude] 1.1); and the Künneth formula for ⊠ (SGA 4 XVII 5.4.3) with D(K ⊠ L) ≅ DK ⊠ DL (BBD 4.2.7).
